A 47-year-old man comes to the office for follow-up of hypertension and diet-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus.  Family medical history is unremarkable.  The patient does not use tobacco, alcohol, or recreational drugs.  Temperature is 37.2 C (99 F), blood pressure is 153/82 mm Hg, pulse is 80/min, and respirations are 14/min.  BMI is 57 kg/m2.  Physical examination shows no abnormalities except obesity.  Laboratory studies show elevated liver transaminases.  The findings from a liver biopsy are shown in the image below:

Which of the following factors most likely contributed to the development of this patient's abnormal histologic findings?​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​

options.label: B
options.text: Decreased hepatic uptake of free fatty acids

explanation:
This patient with obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus has elevated transaminases and a liver biopsy demonstrating hepatic steatosis (ie, fat-containing vacuoles within hepatocytes).  In the absence of alcohol use, this presentation is consistent with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, formerly nonalcoholic fatty liver disease).  MASLD is most common in patients with metabolic syndrome (ie, central obesity, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, hypertension) and significant insulin resistance.

Insulin is released after meals to facilitate storage of recently ingested nutrients (eg, glucose, fatty acids).  It normally promotes glycogen storage and lipogenesis in hepatocytes, stimulates the uptake of triglycerides in adipose tissue, and opposes lipolysis (eg, inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase).

However, in patients with MASLD, resistance to the effects of insulin leads to increased lipolysis in adipose tissue, liberating free fatty acids that are then taken up by hepatocytes.  MASLD is also characterized by increased conversion of carbohydrates and proteins into triglycerides (ie, de novo hepatic lipogenesis increases) despite the insulin resistance due to alterations in the hepatocellular insulin response, which further contributes to steatosis.  The excess quantities of hepatic fat lead to oxidative damage, inflammation, and possible fibrosis and scarring (ie, cirrhosis).  The mainstay of therapy is weight loss, which can reverse MASLD-related liver damage.

(Choice A)  Insulin normally suppresses gluconeogenesis.  However, gluconeogenesis is increased in patients with MASLD due to insulin resistance and excessive release of glycerin (gluconeogenetic substrate) from adipose tissue.

(Choice B)  Insulin resistance results in increased (not decreased) hepatic uptake of free fatty acids.  The uptake of fatty acids normally leads to increased beta-oxidation (ie, fatty acid breakdown) in hepatocyte mitochondria, preventing lipids from accumulating.  However, in patients with MASLD, most of the absorbed fatty acids are shunted toward triglyceride synthesis, exacerbating the steatosis.

(Choice C)  Hemochromatosis is characterized by excessive absorption of dietary iron and subsequent deposition of iron in various tissues.  Deposition of iron in the pancreas can injure the beta cells, leading to diabetes mellitus.  However, hepatic iron deposition manifests as brown deposits that stain strongly with Prussian blue rather than the formation of large fat droplets.

Educational objective:Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is a common complication of metabolic syndrome and insulin resistance.  Insulin resistance leads to increased lipolysis in adipose tissue, releasing free fatty acids that are then taken up by hepatocytes.  Excessive intrahepatic accumulation of toxic lipids causes oxidative damage and inflammation and can eventually result in fibrosis and scarring (ie, cirrhosis).​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​
